this isn’t sponsored, but i wanna tell you how much i love this hotel! 
this is my third time staying there, and each time has been wonderful! 
for anyone with kids who knows they’ll be out and about most of their trip and wants a clean, safe hotel to return to at night, this is for you! 
it’s modern, fun, and has all the best amenities without being overly expensive!
you get a $20 daily credit and we love using it at the main (street level) Cafe d’AVIGNON ! you also get a delicious complimentary coffee bar from 7-10 each day and the bathrooms on the 2nd floor are immaculate.
if the room isn’t ready upon arrival, just ask them to check your bags! and if you’re a marriott gold member (automatic for Amex Plat holders) you get late checkout at 2pm!! 
plus the foosball table and sitting area on the second floor are so fun. 
there’s a barbershop on the bottom floor and really amazing club on the top floor too that has amazing views of the city!! 
while of course this hotel isn’t the most kid oriented hotel since that’s not their audience, it didn’t bother us one bit. the kids were treated so kindly and even given a sweet gift upon checkout!
i’m a very light sleeper and just requested a middle - lower floor hotel room so the rooftop night scene wasn’t that bothersome, and with some white noise on spotify, we slept just fine! honestly the street sirens were louder than the music!

anyways, 10/10 recommend and we will def be back!
plus, the room bathrooms are my favorite!!! 

oh and! sorry i keep remembering things and this is how i type 😂
the location is KEY!!!
we get to walk there from the train station not using any taxis or Ubers and since i’m such a brilliant light packer now 😂 (1 suitcase for 4 of us!) it was super easy to get to and from.

we then walked back to Moynihan Train Hall and you HAVE to have lunch there during the holidays! it’s so fun and festive and there are tons of options! it feels like a movie scene. 🥹

another tip : with kids you can board on amtrak first and we got a table near the cafe car which the girls LOVED!

We’re back @moodring with the talented techno DJ & designer, @actuatordj as our guest host 🖤

After meeting through @se_dj_school, one of the things we connected over (at the historic reopening of Paragon with Kevin Saunderson playing), was how important it is to consider all of what we’re a part of not only a cultural renaissance but a political one. One where we gather not just for the hype of playing, but to connect with each other for deeper solidary work together. 

That’s why we’re excited to have @culturalsolidarity joining us. Cultural solidarity is a mutual aid & generative community hub for cultural workers in the imperial core. The group works to spread information about how cultural movements are a core part of nightlife history, and how art spaces can be catalysts for change. Cultural Solidarity supports cultural workers facing repression and/or financial hardship due to their solidarity work and resistance for Palestine or other oppressed groups. 

We put on this free event by accepting a percentage of bar sales. We’ll be donating 50% of proceeds to @culturalsolidarity, and encourage you to donate to a Palestine-focused fundraiser of your choosing (we will provide some examples shortly!).

Come with your crew, a friend, a date—or come solo and meet some people. All levels are welcome! Just bring a USB, a pair of headphones, and whatever sounds you’ve been playing with lately, and connect with fellow local selectors and music lovers.

HOW IT WORKS
~ Sign up with one of your hosts upon arrival
~ 6pm - 8pm: first come first serve, 30 min slots
~ 8pm - 12am: raffle, 20 min slots
~ 2x tickets for FLINTA* DJs 
~ raffle is generally drawn at the top of every hour for the next hour (ex. At 7pm for 8:00, 8:20 & 8:40) 

FLINTA* stands for “Female, Lesbian, Intersex, Nonbinary, Trans, Agender, and * for other gender nonconforming people.” You can tell us to sign you up for 2x tickets if this term describes you!

You can find more info on logistics, equipment, and more on RA.

PARADISE CONTAINER 
January 31st & February 1st 2026
At @pioneerworks 

Staged across a sprawling set that mimics a deconstructed home, Paradise Container tells the story of a family shaped by addiction and financial enmeshment with a storage solutions company that contracts each of its members. Conceived and written by Monica Mirabile and Mara McKevitt , the newly commissioned performance takes place within the Main Hall of Pioneer Works—reimagined here as a cross between a soundstage and an American fulfillment warehouse.

Paradise Container guides the audience from room to room through light, sound, and performance cues. Charged domestic scenes collapse boundaries between the personal, domestic, and professional environments that define daily life. In this universe, an eroding nuclear family must meet the demands of a modern yet feudal work arrangement, navigate the oscillatory effects of a pharmaceutical drug called Shift, and learn how to live with and love each other. An intimate, performance-theater experience intended for only eighty audience members at a time, Paradise Container crafts a narrative meant to chafe at ideas of stability and disillusion, sickness and health, and the myth of work-life balance.
